messages.author: d78ace1b34bb3f73
messages.subject: Time-stratified analysis - error
parts:
Hi Nick,

I am attempting to do a time-stratified analysis, but running into an error that I cannot seem to find a solution to - Error in section_the_tree(inputs = BioGeoBEARS_run_object, make_master_table = TRUE,  : 
  STOP ERROR in section_the_tree(): the timeperiods file *HAS* to have an oldest time that is older than the bottom node in your tree.  Use the function prt() to get a table of node ages for your tree. The oldest node age in your tree is: 61.349266202. The times in your timeperiods file are: .

My analysis includes two time periods (see timeperiods.txt and dispersal_multipliers.txt attached). In short, I want to stratify the analysis into 0-30 my and 30 my to the root of my tree. I have checked several things, but I must be missing something because I can't get passed this error:

1) I have specified in the timeperiods.txt file an age (100) that is older than my root at 61.34 my. These times are reasonable given my study organism;

2) I have checked using my text editor (sublime) that the tabs and spacing in both the timeperiods.txt and dispersal_multipliers.txt files are similar to those in your example files from Ree and Smith;

3) The timeperiods.txt and dispersal_multipliers.txt files are in my working directory;

4) I have uncommented the following lines:
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$timesfn = "timeperiods.txt"
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$dispersal_multipliers_fn = "dispersal_multipliers.txt"

BioGeoBEARS_run_object = section_the_tree(inputs=BioGeoBEARS_run_object, make_master_table=TRUE, plot_pieces=FALSE)


I have deliberately filled the dispersal_multipliers.txt file with 1's, as I would like to get this working before I move forward.

I have looked through the suggestions given throughout the google group, but have yet to find something that helps with this small problem. I usually am able to trouble-shoot through these types of errors, but this one is being too pesky.

Thanks for your time,
Tammy

Hi all!

Apologies for the trouble with this 

Everything is running for me just fine, and I just re-installed from GitHub just to be sure.  I am attaching the files & script I used.

That error message does suggest that nothing is being read from timeperiods.txt, because normally it would say e.g. "The times in your timeperiods file are: 30 100." or something like that.

My best guess it is something to do with an operating system like Windows mis-reading line-endings, or some such(?)

You can check just the reading/loading of the timeperiods file with:

timeperiods = read_times_fn(inputs=NULL, timesfn="timeperiods.txt")

For me, this returns:

...which seems correct.

I'm attaching all of the files I used (just yours, renamed in some cases).

Nick

BioGeoBEARS_run_object = readfiles_BioGeoBEARS_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object)
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$timesfn = time_stratified_fn

instead of 

BioGeoBEARS_run_object$timesfn = time_stratified_fn  
BioGeoBEARS_run_object = readfiles_BioGeoBEARS_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object)

Ivan
